funnel.title: The funnel: 800 designs in, 20 designs out
funnel.subtitle: Green chips are free CPU screens that run in seconds, orange chips cost GPU minutes, and the pink chip is the expensive verification round - every design re-folded five times against the full 409-residue receptor

generation.heading: Generation - 800 scored designs
generation.sub: five independent generators plus one re-sequencer, all conditioned on the ECD-TMD junction or deeper; counts from records/selection-scores-2026-10-23.csv

slices.label: RFD4-Proteina · 401
slices.legend: RFD4-Proteina (hosted, NVIDIA's free GPU pool): three rounds - the deep message region at 60-100 aa (256), the ECD-TMD junction block K197/Q210/Q221/Q234 (73), the deep region at 40-70 aa (72)

slices.label: SolubleMPNN · 154
slices.legend: SolubleMPNN re-sequencing: not a generator - champion backbones re-sequenced with the interface pinned and only the periphery redesigned (40 + 33 + 81)

slices.label: BoltzGen · 145
slices.legend: BoltzGen 0.3.2: cyclic peptides on the junction constraint (55), the 20-24 aa length class (30), the junction recipe at 60-design scale (60)

slices.label: RFdiffusion3 · 67
slices.legend: RFdiffusion3: miniproteins, contig 60-100, first against groove+junction hotspots and then against the junction alone - the comparison that produced the split rule

slices.label: BindCraft2 · 18
slices.legend: BindCraft2: 15-18 aa peptides at the junction, its own gates relaxed so that raw output reaches our independent screen (it accepted 0 of 50)

slices.label: EvoBind · 15
slices.legend: EvoBind: peptides designed from sequence alone, no backbone and no template - the only route whose GLP1R designs have activated the receptor in published cAMP assays

steps.title: Co-fold against the full receptor
steps.text: Boltz-2 2.2.1, 5 diffusion samples per design, seed 42, binder as chain A and the whole 409-residue construct as chain B, receptor MSA depth-capped at 1024 rows. Never a cut-down target: a binder designed against the extracellular domain alone clashes into the omitted transmembrane bundle. The uncapped server MSA needed 14.65 GiB and was killed; capped, a fold runs about 90 s at ~11.7 GiB.
steps.cost: expensive - GPU hours, 5 models per design

steps.heading: 800 designs, five models each
steps.sub: one shared pipeline, so every generator's output is scored by the same script with the same settings

steps.title: Two-domain binding screen
steps.text: Per sample: ipSAE >= 0.80 (the line calibrated in challenge 2) AND at least one groove residue within 4.5 A AND at least one TM-pocket residue within 4.5 A AND zero atom pairs closer than 2.0 A. Contacts decide where a design binds; confidence never substitutes. Run by campaigns/c1-two-domain/scripts/screen_folds_c3.py.

steps.heading: 222 two-domain HITs
steps.sub: a high ipSAE on the groove alone is labelled groove-only - the published antagonist outcome

steps.title: Activation-geometry gate
steps.text: Six GLP-1 message-region contacts (an anion to R190, an aromatic at Y148, a small group at W306, an H-bond to Q234, a hydrophobe at E387, ECL3 contact) plus the insertion depth below the vestibule-rim centroid. Cutoffs declared before any design existed and calibrated on four experimental structures: 6X18 GLP-1 reads 6/6 at 20.59 A, the groove-only control 0/6 at 7.3 A. Run on all five samples per design by campaigns/c8-deep-junction/scripts/rescore-all.py.

steps.heading: 87 designs carry the full 6/6 pattern
steps.sub: the gate also reports pose agreement: how many of the five samples land in the deep tier

steps.title: Wrap-pose check
steps.text: A binder lying across the receptor can collect deep contacts without inserting anything. The hormone-footprint lens (19 reference contacts from 6X18) exposed the class: three of the four designs that reached the pool's ceiling of 6 of 19 were wrapping at depths of 57-74 A. Beyond the declared 30 A threshold a design loses a full point of activation credit.

steps.heading: Wrapping poses penalised, not trusted
steps.sub: pool ceiling on the harsh lens is 6 of 19; the ranking's leaders reproduce 3 to 5

steps.title: Hard quality floors
steps.text: Applied before ranking, because the composite under-weights what makes a design untestable: no design below 63 pLDDT, none below 0.18 pDockQ2, and no low-complexity sequence (residue entropy below 2.5 bits, a single residue above 45 % of the chain, or a homopolymer run of 6 or more). The floors exist because the selector once returned a 24-residue poly-alanine tract that scored 88.4.

steps.heading: 486 removed, 314 eligible
steps.sub: the floors cut more than half the pool before a single design is ranked

steps.title: Composite ranking and de-duplication
steps.text: total = 2*A + 1.5*B + 1*E + 0.5*R, each term capped at 5.0: A is activation evidence (6/6 with strong pose agreement = 5), B is binding on ipSAE bands with a bonus at pDockQ2 >= 0.30, E is expression risk from pLDDT and hydropathy bands, R is the fraction of the groove / TM-pocket / ECL3 path recovered. Activation outweighs binding because the organizers' prompt says evidence for the hardest goal wins. Any sequence >= 90 % identical to one already kept is rejected; the family count breaks ties only.

steps.heading: Top 20 by score
steps.sub: the cut is tight: the twentieth entry scores 87.8 and the first design below the line scores 87.8 on a total 0.02 lower

steps.title: The organizers' prescreen
steps.text: adaptyvbio/binder-prescreen against its 225-entry GLP1R reference set (215 GLP-1 analogue peptides, 7 antibody chains, 3 peptide-Fc fusions): 18 pass and 2 return no_reference_signal - both peptides under the tool's documented 25-residue floor. Target similarity 0.00 on nineteen entries, every cluster size 1.

steps.heading: Zero flags
steps.sub: no entry is a known binder or a near-match to one

final.heading: 20 designs submitted
final.sub: 13 to 96 residues; 17 at the full 6/6 activation pattern and 3 at 5/6; insertion depths 17.6 to 29.3 A around the hormone's own 20.6 A; six method families

note.title: The loop that fed champions back in.
note.text: Interface-pinned SolubleMPNN re-sequencing ran three times on backbones that had already passed the gate - campaign 1's champions (40 variants), the one c1 design with the full 6/6 geometry (33), and all 27 full-geometry RFD4 champions (81). It is not machine learning: nothing is trained, the interface residues within 4 A are held fixed so the pose survives by construction, and every child is judged by the same fold-and-score instruments as its parent. The third pass returned 25 full-geometry variants from 81 - a 31 % rate, the highest of any single pass in the challenge, generator rounds included.

molecular_figures.caption: The same epitope reached three ways. Left: c13-junction-b43-d02, the 96-residue junction-conditioned RFD4 champion that leads the submission (6/6 at 19.2 A, all five samples deep, ipSAE 0.918). Middle: c2-run1-b206, the 15-residue EvoBind peptide that reproduces the full pattern at 20.6 A - the hormone's own depth in 6X18 is 20.59 A. Right: e1-r0025, the 66-residue RFdiffusion3 miniprotein with the pool's highest ipSAE at 0.933 and 5 of 6 contacts. The receptor is the same full 409-residue construct in all three panels; the designs differ by a factor of six in size and land in the same place.

panels.label: c2-run1-b206 - 15 aa EvoBind peptide, 6/6 at 20.6 A

molecular_figures.caption: The re-sequencing loop in one picture. Left: c12-b21-d08, the 81-residue RFD4-Proteina champion (6/6 at 20.1 A, 5/5 pose agreement, ipSAE 0.869). Right: c12-mpnn-b21-d08-v1, the interface-pinned SolubleMPNN variant of the same backbone - the interface residues within 4 A are held fixed and only the periphery is redesigned, so the pose is preserved by construction (6/6 at 20.3 A, 5/5, ipSAE 0.869, pLDDT 79.8 against the parent's 79.1). Both are in the submitted twenty; this pass produced the best full-geometry yield of the challenge, 25 of 81.
